qualitative.gate_2_reason: Operating income and assets are overwhelmingly concentrated in non-Western emerging markets across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East (>75%), exposing earnings to severe geopolitical realignment, currency volatility, and non-Western legal and regulatory risks.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (REJECT). Standard Chartered is a UK-headquartered bank whose business is overwhelmingly concentrated in non-Western emerging markets across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East (>75% of operating profit), failing the Western essential need standard and carrying heavy geopolitical, sanctions-compliance, and EM sovereign credit risk.
qualitative.evidence: Corporate segment reporting confirms Greater China & North Asia, ASEAN & South Asia, and Africa & Middle East generate over three-quarters of operating income and risk-weighted assets. Historic multi-billion-dollar regulatory penalties for sanctions violations (US DOJ/OFAC) and recurring credit loss provisions in China commercial real estate demonstrate the heightened geopolitical and jurisdictional risk.
